subject: tu:game/movie/movieplayer
value:
PREMISE CORRECTION, MEASURED: movieplayer's two data flip blockers were NOT a failure to emit and NOT a claim-slack site -- splits.txt simply never claimed the TU's read-only data at all, and our object's bytes were already correct. The work_claim framing ('find what our build FAILS TO EMIT ... spell the literals', citing the auxanim extern-ghost corruption class) is refuted by the direction of the datadiff line itself: `target 0x0 vs ours 0x16C` means we emit and the SPLIT owns nothing, which is the opposite of a ghost. Read the direction before choosing a lever.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE WAS, all cheap and all before any build. movieplayer.cpp's splits.txt entry listed only extab/extabindex/.text. `objdump -h` on the split object confirmed it has no .rodata and no .sdata2 sections whatsoever. The unclaimed .rodata run 0x80117528..0x80117698 is bounded exactly by the previous symbol's end (lbl_801174B4 + 0x74) and by cardutil's claimed start, and its split listing (build/GUNE5D/asm/auto_06_801174A8_rodata.s) is byte-for-byte our object's .rodata: a 0x100 path buffer opening "Gauntlet/VQMovies/@", then "Gauntlet/VQMovies/midway.avi", "MoviePlayer", "MoviePlayerBase", "Gauntlet/VQMovies/KnotVQ.avi", "MoviePlayer.cpp". Link order corroborates independently: the entry directly above movieplayer (g3dpad.c) ends its .sdata2 at exactly 0x80349390, where movieplayer's begins, and adstream.c owns the .rodata immediately below.

RESOLUTION 1, .rodata, FULLY CLOSED: claim 0x80117528..0x80117694 and shrink lbl_80117654 from 0x44 to 0x40. The trailing 4 zero bytes are link alignment padding for cardutil's 8-aligned start, and this is exactly case (b) of the slack-ownership law -- the last declared symbol's size overran our object's true end, so shrinking BOTH recovers full credit. Result +364 matched data bytes (0x16C), section 100.0% equal.

RESOLUTION 2, .sdata2, PARTIALLY CLOSED AND THE REMAINDER IS STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE. The TU's real pool is the whole unclaimed 0x68 block 0x80349390..0x803493F8, proven by the target object's own relocations (it references lbl_80349390/94/98/9C/A0/A8/B0/B8/BC/D8/DC/E0/E4/E8/EC/F0 and nothing outside it; an all-objects sweep found no other real TU referencing them). Our object emits only 0x10 of it -- the two MWCC int-to-double magic doubles -- and those are byte-identical to the target's pair at 0x803493A8/0x803493B0, so claiming exactly that 0x10 subrange makes the section 100.0% equal (+16 bytes) and clears the blocker. THE REST CANNOT BE EMITTED: offsets 0x30..0x46 of that block are the CodeWarrior RTTI class-name strings "VQCodec", "Codec", and a second "Codec" (the duplicate-per-referencing-context signature). Our cflags carry `-RTTI off`; more decisively, a direct `-RTTI on` probe on this TU produced a byte-identical object with no new sections at all, because the recipe in claim.law.destructor-throw-spec-adds-a-second-unexpected-island deliberately spells these polymorphic classes NON-virtual so MWCC emits no `__vt__` into a TU whose split owns no .data. Emitting the RTTI strings would require real `virtual` members, which would emit vtable and RTTI objects into unclaimed .data/.sdata -- trading one cleared blocker for two larger ones and breaking the destructors that recipe already made exact. So the 0x58 remainder is a deliberate, recorded consequence of the destructor recipe, not an open task.
